record.original_question: For a field F and positive integer n, is the n-torsion subgroup nBr(F) generated by Brauer classes of cyclic algebras of degree dividing n?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1. [Alb36, p. 126] Is the n-torsion subgroup nBr(F) generated by the classes of cyclic algebras of degree (dividing) n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and $n$ a positive integer. Recall that the Brauer group $\mathrm{Br}(F)$ is the group of equivalence classes of finite-dimensional central simple $F$-algebras under tensor product, where two such algebras are equivalent if they have isomorphic matrix algebras over a common division algebra. Let ${}_n\mathrm{Br}(F) = \{[A] \in \mathrm{Br}(F) : n \cdot [A] = 0\}$ denote the $n$-torsion subgroup.

A central simple $F$-algebra $A$ of degree $m$ (i.e., $\dim_F A = m^2$) is called cyclic if it contains a maximal commutative subfield $L \subset A$ such that $L/F$ is a cyclic Galois extension of degree $m$. Equivalently, $A \cong (L/F,\sigma,a)$ for some generator $\sigma$ of $\mathrm{Gal}(L/F)$ and some $a \in F^\times$.

Question: Is ${}_n\mathrm{Br}(F)$ generated, as an abelian group, by the Brauer classes of cyclic $F$-algebras of degree dividing $n$? Equivalently, can every $n$-torsion Brauer class over $F$ be written as a sum of classes of cyclic algebras of degree dividing $n$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question, going back to Albert (1936), is classical. By the Merkurjev–Suslin theorem, if $F$ contains a primitive $n$th root of unity then ${}_n\mathrm{Br}(F)$ is generated by cyclic (symbol) algebras of degree $n$. Without this hypothesis, the problem remains open in general; positive results are known in special cases (e.g., small $n$, particular classes of fields such as global/local fields), but no general answer is known.

status_evidence.snippet: Problem 3.1 (Albert 1936): Is the n-torsion subgroup nBr(F) generated by the classes of cyclic algebras of degree (dividing) n?
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed as an open problem of Albert in a survey on central simple algebras.

status_evidence.title: Is the Brauer group generated by cyclic algebras?
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of whether classes in the Brauer group can be represented by cyclic algebras; problem remains open in general.
status_evidence.claim: The question of cyclic generation of the Brauer group is treated as an open problem with partial results.

status_evidence.title: Brauer group - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: By Merkurjev–Suslin, when F contains a primitive nth root of unity, the n-torsion of Br(F) is generated by classes of cyclic algebras of degree n.
status_evidence.claim: Generation by cyclic algebras is known under a roots-of-unity assumption (Merkurjev–Suslin).
